rules: You control Q*bert from the JSON state only. The objective is to change the top of EVERY pyramid cube to the current destination color, then continue on the next round. The destination color is target_color in the JSON. The board contains six rows: r0c0 at the top, and row r has columns c0 through cr from left to right. Atari joystick labels are rotated relative to the screen: UP hops screen up-right to (r-1,c); LEFT hops screen up-left to (r-1,c-1); RIGHT hops screen down-right to (r+1,c+1); DOWN hops screen down-left to (r+1,c). The JSON legal_actions already excludes hops off the pyramid. NOOP and FIRE do not select a hop. Each selected input is released as soon as Q*bert first appears on a different tile; the emulator then receives NOOP until his position settles before the next decision. On the initial level a hop changes a starting-color cube to the destination color, and another visit leaves it there. Later levels may require two visits through an intermediate color, or may revert a cube on another visit. Use tile_colors and target_color from this observation; do not assume a color always means one visit across every level. Q*bert is the orange player. A purple ball or purple snake is dangerous. Red balls are dangerous. Sam and the green ball are not collision hazards, though Sam can undo cube progress. The extractor currently reports only purple enemies in JSON; an empty enemies list does not prove all hazards are absent. Avoid reported enemy positions and preserve lives. Use recent_moves to avoid repeating a zero-progress loop. From an already completed cube, move toward a nearby cube whose color differs from target_color. If candidate_next_states is present, it projects each legal landing tile from the movement rules. Choose a safe action with a new color change when available; otherwise choose a route closer to unfinished cubes. The projection is geometric and does not predict enemy motion or delayed score updates. The actual state will be supplied after every move. Choose exactly one action from the catalogue.
state_source: vision model on one unchanged frame for cube colors, Q*bert, enemies, score, and spare lives; fixed game rules and observed action/reward history for the remaining JSON fields; scripted RGB and ALE info used only for scoring and emulator timing
